   140→
   141→## Architecture
   142→
   143→### Data Flow (MCP to Houdini)
   144→
   145→```
   146→ANY MCP Client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, custom agents)
   147→    |  Streamable HTTP: POST/GET http://localhost:PORT/mcp
   148→    |  JSON-RPC 2.0 + Mcp-Session-Id headers
   149→    |
   150→MCP Protocol Layer  (synapse/mcp/)
   151→    |  Session mgmt, tool/resource/prompt dispatch
   152→    |  Translates JSON-RPC ↔ SYNAPSE commands
   153→    |
   154→    ├─── tools/call ──────┐
   155→    ├─── resources/read ──┤
   156→    └─── prompts/get ─────┤
   157→                          |
   158→Claude Desktop/Code       |  (existing stdio path preserved)
   159→    |  stdio / JSON-RPC   |
   160→mcp_server.py  (61 tools) |
   161→    |                     |
   162→    ├─────────────────────┘
   163→    |  WebSocket: ws://localhost:9999/synapse
   164→SynapseServer  (daemon thread inside Houdini)
   165→    |  CommandHandlerRegistry (handlers.py)
   166→hou.* Python API
   167→    |
   168→Houdini USD Stage / Solaris / Karma
   169→```
   170→
   171→Both MCP Streamable HTTP and the existing WebSocket/stdio paths converge at the same handler layer. The MCP protocol layer adds no new safety logic — it delegates entirely to existing handlers which enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions.
   172→
   173→### Core Package Layout (`python/synapse/`)
   174→
   175→| Layer | Directory | Responsibility |
   176→|-------|-----------|---------------|
   177→| Foundation | `core/` | Wire protocol (`protocol.py`), parameter aliases (`aliases.py`), determinism (`determinism.py`), audit chain (`audit.py`), human gates (`gates.py`), encryption (`crypto.py`), command queue (`queue.py`) |
   178→| Memory | `memory/` | JSONL store (`store.py`) or SQLite store (`sqlite_store.py`, via `SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND=sqlite`), data models (`models.py`), shot context (`context.py`), markdown export (`markdown.py`), **Living Memory**: scene memory (`scene_memory.py`), agent state USD (`agent_state.py`), evolution system (`evolution.py`) |
   179→| Routing | `routing/` | Tiered LLM dispatch (`router.py`), regex parser (`parser.py`), RAG knowledge (`knowledge.py`), recipes (`recipes.py`), deterministic cache (`cache.py`), workflow planner (`planner.py`), epoch-based tier adaptation (`adaptation.py`) |
   180→| Agent | `agent/` | prepare/propose/execute/learn lifecycle (`executor.py`), task/plan/step protocol (`protocol.py`), outcome tracking (`learning.py`) |
   181→| MCP | `mcp/` | MCP Streamable HTTP protocol layer. `server.py` (endpoint handler, JSON-RPC router), `session.py` (session manager), `tools.py` (tool registry, 61 tools), `resources.py` (scene state resources), `prompts.py` (workflow prompts), `protocol.py` (JSON-RPC utilities, error codes), `types.py` (type definitions, schemas) |
   182→| Server | `server/` | WebSocket server (`websocket.py`), command handlers split across 7 files: `handlers.py` (core registry + 18 handlers), `handlers_render.py` (viewport/render/keyframe/settings/validation/farm), `handlers_tops.py` (wedge + 15 tops_* PDG handlers), `handlers_material.py` (create/assign/read material), `handlers_memory.py` (memory/context), `handlers_node.py` (node ops), `handlers_usd.py` (USD/Solaris). Shared utilities in `handler_helpers.py`. Plus: resilience stack (`resilience.py`), introspection (`introspection.py`), hwebserver adapter (`hwebserver_adapter.py`), REST adapter (`api_adapter.py`), guards (`guards.py`), auth (`auth.py`), metrics (`metrics.py`), RBAC (`rbac.py`), multi-user sessions (`sessions.py`), live metrics (`live_metrics.py`), dashboard (`dashboard.py`), render farm (`render_farm.py`, `render_farm_handler.py`), render diagnostics (`render_diagnostics.py`), render notifications (`render_notify.py`) |
   183→| Session | `session/` | SynapseBridge singleton hub (`tracker.py`), session summaries (`summary.py`) |
   184→| UI | `ui/` | Qt panel with 5 tabs (`panel.py`), tab widgets in `tabs/` |
   185→
   186→### Routing Cascade (cheapest-first)
   187→
   188→```
   189→Cache(O(1)) -> Recipe(O(1)) -> Planner(O(1)) -> Tier0/regex(O(n)) -> Tier1/RAG(O(log n)) -> Tier2/Haiku(~5s) -> Tier3/Agent(~15s)
   190→```
   191→
   192→- **Tier pinning** (He2025 consistency): Same input+context maps to same tier on subsequent calls. LRU cache, max 1,000 pins, stale pins fall through.
   193→- **Speculative T0+T1 parallelism**: Module-level `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` runs Tier 0 regex and Tier 1 knowledge lookup concurrently.
   194→- **Tier 1 result threading**: `route()` runs `knowledge.lookup()` once, threads the result to all higher tiers to avoid redundant lookups.
   195→
   196→### Transport Backends
   197→
   198→| Backend | Module | Transport | Latency | Use Case |
   199→|---------|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
   200→| `websockets` | `server/websocket.py` | WebSocket | ~0.2ms warm ping | Primary — reads, pings, everything |
   201→| `hwebserver` | `server/hwebserver_adapter.py` | HTTP (Houdini native) | ~2s floor (main event loop) | Optional — only for hou.* mutations |
   202→| `mcp` | `mcp/server.py` | Streamable HTTP (MCP) | ~2s (hwebserver) | Universal MCP client access (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) |
   203→
   204→WebSocket remains the primary internal transport. The MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is additive — it provides a standardized protocol interface that any MCP-compliant client can use. Both share the same handler layer.
   205→
   206→### Authentication (`server/auth.py`)
   207→
   208→Optional API key authentication for both transports. Key sources (checked in order):
   209→1. `SYNAPSE_API_KEY` environment variable
   210→2. `~/.synapse/auth.key` file (first non-empty, non-comment line)
   211→3. No key configured -> auth disabled (backward compat)
   212→
   213→When enabled, first WebSocket message must be an `authenticate` command with `{"payload": {"key": "..."}}`. Uses `hmac.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison. Auth handshake integrated into both `websocket.py` and `hwebserver_adapter.py`.
   214→
   215→**MCP auth (Phase 3):** Bearer token authentication via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on the `/mcp` endpoint. Opt-in for remote/studio deployments. Not required for localhost connections. Implemented as a `TokenVerifier` that delegates to the existing `auth.py` key validation.
   216→
   217→### MCP Server — stdio Bridge (`mcp_server.py`)
   218→
   219→61 tools (24 houdini_, 23 synapse_, 14 tops_). Key operational details:
   220→- **Concurrent dispatch**: `_pending` dict + `_recv_loop` coroutine — no blocking lock, true parallel tool calls
   221→- **Timeouts**: Default 10s. Overrides: execute_python/execute_vex/capture_viewport/inspect_* at 30s, render/wedge at 120s, batch at 60s
   222→- **JSON**: Uses `orjson` (fast, sort_keys via `OPT_SORT_KEYS`) when available, falls back to stdlib `json`
   223→- **Warmup**: Pre-connect in `main()` reduces first-call latency
   224→- **Retry**: `MAX_RETRIES=2`, `RETRY_DELAY=0.3`, auto-retry on connection drop
   225→- **Connection**: `open_timeout=3.0`, `ping_interval=None`, `compression=None` (localhost optimization)
   226→
   227→The stdio MCP bridge (`mcp_server.py`) and the Streamable HTTP layer (`synapse/mcp/`) are separate transports sharing the same handler layer.
   228→
   229→### MCP Protocol Layer — Streamable HTTP
   230→
   231→The MCP protocol layer lives in `synapse/mcp/` and provides a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint at `/mcp` on the hwebserver.
   232→
   233→#### Endpoint Behavior
   234→
   235→```
   236→POST /mcp   →  Client sends JSON-RPC request or notification
   237→               Response: application/json (single result) or text/event-stream (streaming)
   238→GET  /mcp   →  Opens optional SSE stream for server→client messages (Phase 3)
   239→```
   240→
   241→#### Session Lifecycle
   242→
   243→1. Client POSTs `initialize` with `clientInfo` and `protocolVersion`
   244→2. Server responds with capabilities, serverInfo, and `Mcp-Session-Id` header
   245→3. Client sends `notifications/initialized` (server returns 202 Accepted)
   246→4. Session is live — client can call `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/read`, etc.
   247→5. Session ends when client disconnects or sends `notifications/cancelled`
   248→
   249→#### Initialize Response
   250→
   251→```python
   252→{
   253→    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
   254→    "capabilities": {
   255→        "tools": {"listChanged": True},
   256→        "resources": {"subscribe": False, "listChanged": False},
   257→    },
   258→    "serverInfo": {
   259→        "name": "synapse",
   260→        "version": "5.4.0"
   261→    },
   262→    "instructions": (
   263→        "SYNAPSE is a bridge between AI agents and SideFX Houdini. "
   264→        "All mutations go through safety middleware enforcing atomic scripts, "
   265→        "idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. "
   266→        "Tools marked destructiveHint=True modify the Houdini scene."
   267→    )
   268→}
   269→```
   270→
   271→#### Tool Registry — Mapping Existing Handlers
   272→
   273→Every existing SYNAPSE command handler maps 1:1 to an MCP tool. The `synapse/mcp/tools.py` module builds `tools/list` output from handler introspection and dispatches `tools/call` to the handler registry.
   274→
   275→Tool definitions include JSON Schema `inputSchema` and MCP `annotations`:
   276→
   277→```python
   278→{
   279→    "name": "execute_vex",
   280→    "description": "Execute VEX code on a wrangle node through SYNAPSE safety middleware.",
   281→    "inputSchema": {
   282→        "type": "object",
   283→        "properties": {
   284→            "code": {"type": "string", "description": "VEX source code"},
   285→            "node_path": {"type": "string", "description": "Full path to wrangle node"},
   286→            "run_over": {
   287→                "type": "string",
   288→                "enum": ["Points", "Vertices", "Primitives", "Detail"],
   289→                "default": "Points"
   290→            }
   291→        },
   292→        "required": ["code", "node_path"]
   293→    },
   294→    "annotations": {
   295→        "title": "Execute VEX Code",
   296→        "readOnlyHint": False,
   297→        "destructiveHint": True,
   298→        "idempotentHint": False,
   299→        "openWorldHint": False
   300→    }
   301→}
   302→```
   303→
   304→**Annotation rules:** Use `readOnlyHint: True` for all read/inspect/get operations. Use `destructiveHint: True` for anything that modifies the scene. Use `idempotentHint: True` for set operations where repeat calls produce the same result. MCP clients use these for UI gating and safety decisions.
   305→
   306→#### Tool Dispatch — Bridge to Handlers
   307→
   308→```python
   309→async def dispatch_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict) -> dict:
   310→    """Bridge MCP tools/call to existing SYNAPSE handlers.
   311→    Safety middleware is enforced by the handlers — NOT bypassed."""
   312→    handler = HANDLER_REGISTRY.get(tool_name)
   313→    if not handler:
   314→        raise MCPError(-32602, f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}")
   315→    try:
   316→        result = await handler(arguments)
   317→        return {
   318→            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(result) if isinstance(result, dict) else str(result)}]
   319→        }
   320→    except SynapseError as e:
   321→        return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"Error: {e.message}"}], "isError": True}
   322→```
   323→
   324→**CRITICAL:** `dispatch_tool` implements zero safety logic. It delegates to existing handlers which already enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. The MCP layer is a thin protocol translation.
   325→
   326→#### Resources — Scene State Exposure
   327→
   328→Resources provide read-only browseable data. These map to existing introspection capabilities:
   329→
   330→| URI | Description | Backed By |
   331→|-----|-------------|-----------|
   332→| `houdini://scene/info` | Hip file, frame range, FPS, statistics | `get_scene_info` handler |
   333→| `houdini://scene/tree` | Full node hierarchy | `inspect_scene` handler |
   334→| `houdini://node/{path}/parameters` | All parameter values for a node | `get_parm` / `inspect_node` |
   335→| `houdini://node/{path}/attributes` | Geometry attribute metadata + samples | `inspect_node` handler |
   336→| `houdini://node/{path}/cook-stats` | Cook time, memory, dependencies | `get_metrics` handler |
   337→| `houdini://stage/info` | USD stage summary | `get_stage_info` handler |
   338→
   339→URIs with `{path}` are resource templates — the client fills in the parameter.
   340→
   341→#### Prompts — Reusable Workflows (Phase 2)
   342→
   343→| Prompt | Description |
   344→|--------|-------------|
   345→| `vex_debug` | Inspect wrangle inputs, run code, check outputs |
   346→| `lighting_setup` | Standard 3-point rig with proper exposure values |
   347→| `scene_audit` | Check for unnamed nodes, missing textures, heavy geo |
   348→| `render_validation` | Progressive render pipeline (low → high quality) |
   349→
   350→#### JSON-RPC Error Codes
   351→
   352→| Code | Meaning | When |
   353→|------|---------|------|
   354→| -32700 | Parse error | Invalid JSON |
   355→| -32600 | Invalid Request | Missing jsonrpc/method |
   356→| -32601 | Method not found | Unknown MCP method |
   357→| -32602 | Invalid params | Bad tool arguments |
   358→| -32603 | Internal error | Houdini crash, unexpected exception |
   359→| -32001 | Safety guard rejection | Middleware blocked operation |
   360→| -32002 | Node not found | Houdini path doesn't exist |
   361→| -32003 | Cook error | Houdini cook failed |
   362→| -32004 | Session invalid | Bad/expired Mcp-Session-Id |
   363→
   364→#### File Organization
   365→
   366→```
   367→synapse/
   368→├── mcp/                          # MCP Streamable HTTP protocol
   369→│   ├── __init__.py
   370→│   ├── server.py                 # Endpoint handler, JSON-RPC router, hwebserver registration
   371→│   ├── session.py                # Session manager (create, track, destroy)
   372→│   ├── tools.py                  # Tool registry (maps to existing handlers in handlers.py)
   373→│   ├── resources.py              # Resource definitions and readers
   374→│   ├── prompts.py                # Prompt templates (Phase 2)
   375→│   ├── protocol.py               # JSON-RPC utilities, error codes, response builders
   376→│   └── types.py                  # Type definitions, schemas
   377→├── docs/
   378→│   ├── mcp/
   379→│   │   ├── SETUP.md              # User-facing MCP connection guide
   380→│   │   └── TOPS_INTEGRATION_POINTS.md  # Notes for TOPS resumption (append-only)
   381→│   └── tops/
   382→│       └── PARKING_SNAPSHOT.md   # TOPS state at time of parking
   383→```
   384→
   385→#### Connecting Claude Code
   386→
   387→Once the endpoint is running:
   388→
   389→```bash
   390→# One-time setup
   391→claude mcp add --transport http synapse http://localhost:PORT/mcp
   392→
   393→# Verify
   394→claude mcp list
   395→# Inside Claude Code session:
   396→/mcp
   397→
   398→# For team projects, add .mcp.json at repo root:
   399→# { "synapse": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:PORT/mcp" } }
   400→```
   401→
   402→#### Security
   403→
   404→- **Localhost binding only** by default (`127.0.0.1`, not `0.0.0.0`). Claude Code runs locally.
   405→- **No auth for local** — MCP spec permits authless localhost. Bearer token auth is opt-in (Phase 3) for remote/studio deployment.
   406→- **Origin validation** — validate `Origin` header per MCP spec to mitigate DNS rebinding.
   407→- **Cloud context awareness** — Claude Code sends tool results to Anthropic's API. Scene data (node names, attribute values) transits cloud infrastructure. Document this for users with proprietary scenes.
   408→
   409→### `.synapse` Companion Repos
   410→
   411→**Agent SDK** (`~/.synapse/agent/`): Autonomous VFX co-pilot powered by Claude Opus 4.6. Standard Anthropic tool-use message loop (NOT a separate agent framework). 8 tools via direct WebSocket to Synapse. Safety: atomic mutations, idempotent guards, undo-group rollback. 49 tests.
   412→
   413→**Design System** (`~/.synapse/design/`): Pentagram-style monochromatic design. `tokens.py` (colors, typography, spacing — stdlib-only), `generate_icons.py` (21 SVGs from construction rules), `synapse_styles.py` (Qt stylesheet generator). Primary accent: SIGNAL cyan `#00D4FF`.
   414→
   415→**Houdini Integration** (`~/.synapse/houdini/`): `synapse.shelf` (5 toolbar tools), `synapse_shelf.py` (shelf callbacks — inspect, health check, docs), `synapse_panel.pypanel` (PySide2 panel with status polling).
   416→
   417→**Installer** (`~/.synapse/install.py`): Auto-detects Houdini prefs dir, copies shelf/panel/icons. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--uninstall`.
   418→
   419→## Testing Patterns
   420→
   421→**No Houdini required**: All tests import modules via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, bypassing the `hou` dependency. There is no shared `conftest.py` — each test file creates its own minimal `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules["hou"] = mock_hou`. Some test files (e.g., `test_guards.py`, `test_keyframe_aov.py`) save and restore the original `sys.modules["hou"]` in teardown to prevent cross-test pollution.
   422→
   423→**Patching `hou` in handler tests**: Always patch the module-level reference inside handlers.py, NOT `sys.modules["hou"]`. Patching sys.modules breaks object identity across test files.
   424→
   425→```python
   426→# Correct — patch the handlers module's hou reference
   427→_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou
   428→with patch.object(_handlers_hou, "node", return_value=mock_node):
   429→    ...
   430→
   431→# For attributes missing from the stub
   432→with patch.object(hou, "flipbook", create=True):
   433→    ...
   434→```
   435→
   436→**test_guards.py ordering**: Replaces `sys.modules["hou"]` entirely — has save/restore teardown to prevent pollution. `test_render.py` captures `_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou` to patch the correct object.
   437→
   438→**Error assertions**: Use `"Couldn't find"` (not `"not found"`) — matches coaching tone convention.
   439→
   440→**Windows encoding**: Any test writing files with em-dashes or special chars must use `encoding="utf-8"` (cp1252 breaks).
   441→
   442→**MCP protocol tests**: Test the JSON-RPC router, session management, tool dispatch, and resource reading without Houdini. Mock the handler registry to return canned responses. Verify correct error codes, header handling (`Mcp-Session-Id`, `MCP-Protocol-Version`), and content-type negotiation. Follow the same stub pattern as existing tests.
   443→
   444→## Adding New Functionality
   445→
   446→### Adding a new MCP tool
   447→
   448→1. Add `CommandType` variant in `core/protocol.py`
   449→2. Add handler method `_handle_<name>` in the appropriate handler file (`handlers.py` for core, `handlers_render.py` for render/viewport/keyframe/validation, `handlers_tops.py` for TOPS/PDG, `handlers_material.py` for materials, `handlers_usd.py` for USD, `handlers_memory.py` for memory, `handlers_node.py` for node ops) and register it in `SynapseHandler._register_handlers()`
   450→3. Add parameter aliases in `core/aliases.py` if the tool has new parameter names
   451→4. Add `Tool(...)` entry to `list_tools()` and dispatch case to `call_tool()` in `mcp_server.py` (uses `Server.list_tools()`/`Server.call_tool()` decorators, not `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern). All 61 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   452→5. **Add MCP tool definition in `mcp/tools.py`** — include `inputSchema` (JSON Schema for arguments) and `annotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). The tool dispatches to the same handler registered in step 2.
   453→6. Add timeout override to `_SLOW_COMMANDS` in `mcp_server.py` if >10s expected
   454→7. Write tests — bootstrap a `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules`, import handlers via `importlib`, patch `_handlers_hou` (not `sys.modules["hou"]`). **Also write a test in `test_mcp_protocol.py`** verifying the tool appears in `tools/list` and `tools/call` dispatches correctly.
   455→
   456→**Going forward, steps 5 and 7 (MCP registration + MCP test) are mandatory for all new tools.** The MCP tool registry is now the standard way to expose SYNAPSE functionality to external clients.
   457→
   458→### Adding a routing recipe
   459→
   460→Add to `routing/recipes.py` in the `_register_builtins()` method. 21 recipes (11 basic + 10 production). Recipes are Tier 0.5 — pattern-matched before regex, return multi-step command sequences. For complex workflows, use `execute_python` steps. For dynamic composition with modifiers ("set up X with Y and Z"), add workflow templates to `routing/planner.py`.
   461→
   462→### Adding RAG knowledge
   463→
   464→Add/edit files in `rag/skills/houdini21-reference/*.md` (26 files, ~3,900 lines). Update topic triggers in `rag/documentation/_metadata/semantic_index.json` (28 topics, 400+ triggers).
   465→
   466→## Key Conventions
   467→
   468→**Coaching tone**: Error messages say "Couldn't find node" not "Node not found". Always offer next step. `_suggest_parms(node, name)` provides substring-matched alternatives. See `TONE.md` for the full voice guide.
   469→
   470→**He2025 determinism**: `round_float()` for OUTPUT only — never internal timing. `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization (both stdlib `json.dumps` and `orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS`). `@deterministic` decorator auto-rounds float args. `kahan_sum()` for stable aggregation. Content-based UUIDs via `deterministic_uuid()`. Epoch-based adaptation uses fixed epoch SIZE (not time-based) per He2025.
   471→
   472→**Lazy loading**: `__init__.py` uses `__getattr__` to defer routing/server/UI imports. Optional deps use try/except with `*_AVAILABLE` flags. Keeps Houdini startup fast.
   473→
   474→**Thread safety**: `ReadWriteLock` (writer-priority) in `MemoryStore`. `threading.Lock()` for tier-pin cache. `threading.Event()` for background store loading. `_log_executor` ThreadPoolExecutor(2) for fire-and-forget memory logging.
   475→
   476→**Backwards compat**: All legacy names preserved — `NexusServer`, `EngramMemory`, `HyphaeAuditLog`, etc. Storage auto-migrates from `.nexus/`/`.engram/` to `.synapse/`.
   477→
   478→**Singletons**: `AuditLog`, `HumanGate`, `SynapseBridge`, `CryptoEngine` — accessed via `audit_log()`, `human_gate()`, `get_bridge()`, `get_crypto()`.
   479→
   480→**Error classification**: User errors (`ValueError`, `KeyError`, `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `IndexError`, `NameError`) do NOT trip circuit breaker. Service errors (`TimeoutError`, threading errors, Houdini crashes) DO trip it.
   481→
   482→**Rollback errors in execute_python**: `_ROLLBACK_ERRORS = (NameError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError, IndexError)` trigger auto-undo. Operational errors (RuntimeError, hou.OperationFailed) do NOT — earlier mutations may be valid.
   483→
   484→## Lighting Law (Critical Domain Knowledge)
   485→
   486→**Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 (or below)**. Brightness is controlled by **exposure** (logarithmic, in stops). This applies to ALL PBR renderers (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray).
   487→
   488→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference (`log2(3)`)
   489→- Key:fill ratio 4:1 = 2.0 stops difference (`log2(4)`)
   490→- USD exposure parm: `xn__inputsexposure_vya` (value), `xn__inputsexposure_control_wcb` = `"set"` (enable)
   491→- USD intensity parm: `xn__inputsintensity_i0a` — always 1.0
   492→
   493→## Rendering Guidelines
   494→
   495→When building or rendering Solaris scenes via MCP, follow a progressive validation pipeline — never jump straight to production settings:
   496→
   497→1. **Validate stage first**: After creating geometry, lights, and materials, query the stage to confirm all expected prims exist at correct paths. Use exact prim paths for material assignments (not wildcard patterns like `/**` unless verified).
   498→2. **Test render at low quality**: Start with 256x256 resolution, low pixel samples (4-8), no SSS, no displacement, no denoiser. Confirm the render completes and produces output before scaling up.
   499→3. **Scale incrementally**: Increase resolution and samples in steps. Enable expensive features (SSS, subsurface scattering, denoiser) one at a time.
   500→4. **Never use foreground rendering for heavy scenes**: `soho_foreground=1` blocks Houdini entirely — if the render is slow, the WebSocket server becomes unresponsive and the user must force-kill Houdini.
   501→5. **Verify output paths**: Set `picture` on the Karma LOP AND `outputimage` on the ROP. Check the output directory exists. Use `iconvert.exe` from `$HFS/bin/` for EXR-to-JPEG conversion.
   502→
   503→## Wire Protocol
   504→
   505→Default: `ws://localhost:9999/synapse` | Version: `4.0.0`
   506→MCP endpoint: `http://localhost:PORT/mcp` | Protocol: MCP 2025-06-18 (Streamable HTTP)
   507→
   508→53 registered handlers across 7 handler files:
   509→- **Core (18)**: `ping`, `get_health`, `get_help`, `create_node`, `delete_node`, `connect_nodes`, `get_parm`, `set_parm`, `get_scene_info`, `get_selection`, `execute_python`, `execute_vex`, `batch_commands`, `get_metrics`, `router_stats`, `list_recipes`, `knowledge_lookup`, `capture_viewport`
   510→- **Render (8)**: `capture_viewport`, `render`, `set_keyframe`, `render_settings`, `validate_frame`, `render_sequence`, `render_farm_status`
   511→- **TOPS/PDG (16)**: `wedge`, `tops_get_work_items`, `tops_get_dependency_graph`, `tops_get_cook_stats`, `tops_cook_node`, `tops_generate_items`, `tops_configure_scheduler`, `tops_cancel_cook`, `tops_dirty_node`, `tops_setup_wedge`, `tops_batch_cook`, `tops_query_items`, `tops_cook_and_validate`, `tops_diagnose`, `tops_pipeline_status`
   512→- **Materials (3)**: `create_material`, `assign_material`, `read_material`
   513→- **USD (7)**: `get_stage_info`, `get_usd_attribute`, `set_usd_attribute`, `create_usd_prim`, `modify_usd_prim`, `reference_usd`
   514→- **Node (3)**: `create_node`, `delete_node`, `connect_nodes`
   515→- **Memory (7)**: `context`, `search`, `add_memory`, `decide`, `recall`, `inspect_selection`, `inspect_scene`, `inspect_node`
   516→
   517→All handlers are accessible through WebSocket, stdio MCP, and Streamable HTTP MCP transports. Parameter names resolve through `aliases.py` (38+ mappings) — e.g., `node`, `path`, `node_path` all resolve to canonical `node`.
   518→
   519→## Storage Layout
   520→
   521→```
   522→$HIP/.synapse/           # Per-project memory
   523→  memory.jsonl           # Append-only log (async write buffer: 2s flush / 50-item cap / atexit flush)
   524→  index.json             # Search indices (by_type, by_tag, by_keyword)
   525→  context.md             # Human-editable shot context
   526→  decisions.md           # Decision log
   527→  tasks.md               # Task history
   528→
   529→~/.synapse/              # Global
   530→  audit/                 # Daily JSONL audit logs (hash-chain, tamper-evident)
   531→  gates/                 # Gate proposals (timestamped, immutable)
   532→  encryption.key         # Auto-generated Fernet key (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256)
   533→  agent/                 # Autonomous agent SDK (synapse_agent.py entry point)
   534→  design/                # Design tokens, icon generator, Qt styles
   535→  houdini/               # Shelf, panel, callbacks for Houdini integration
   536→  install.py             # Houdini prefs installer
   537→```
   538→
   539→## Gotchas
   540→
   541→- **matlib.cook(force=True)**: MUST cook materiallibrary before `createNode()` on shader child — without cook, internal subnet doesn't exist and createNode returns None
   542→- **Render output_file kwarg**: Doesn't work for usdrender ROPs — set `outputimage` or `picture` parm directly
   543→- **usdrender loppath**: ROPs in `/out` need `loppath` set to a LOP node — handler auto-discovers display node in `/stage`
   544→- **Karma camera**: Must use USD prim path (`/cameras/render_cam`), not Houdini node path
   545→- **override_res**: String menu `""` / `"scale"` / `"specific"` — not int
   546→- **Viewport capture**: Must use Flipbook API with `hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult()` — `QWidget.grab()` returns black for OpenGL; `executeDeferred()` is fire-and-forget and won't block
   547→- **.pypanel imports**: NEVER nuke `sys.modules` — use `hou.session` guard for one-time import
   548→- **RAG Path import**: Handler uses `from pathlib import Path as _Path` (inline) — global `Path` not available in handlers.py
   549→- **MCP execute_python**: MCP param is `code`, but Synapse handler resolves `content` — payload builder in mcp_server.py maps it
   550→- **SVG icon generation**: XML forbids `--` inside comments; use `|` separator
   551→- **synapse_shelf.py**: Security hooks block `parm.eval()` patterns; use `node.evalParm("parm_name")` method instead
   552→- **Agent SDK websockets**: Must import at module level (not inside connect()) — patch target is `synapse_ws.websockets`
   553→- **Zombie servers**: Multiple SynapseServer instances can linger in Houdini; use `gc.get_objects()` + `_actual_port` to find the active one
   554→- **MCP tool registration (stdio bridge)**: Uses `@server.list_tools()` returning `Tool(...)` list + `@server.call_tool()` dispatcher — NOT the `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern. All 61 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   555→- **MCP tool registration (Streamable HTTP)**: Uses the tool registry in `mcp/tools.py` which maps to the same handlers. Both registries must stay in sync — when adding a tool to `mcp_server.py`, also add it to `mcp/tools.py`
   556→- **MCP session headers**: `Mcp-Session-Id` must be returned on the `initialize` response and included by the client on all subsequent requests. hwebserver header access may require case-insensitive lookup
   557→- **MCP notifications return 202**: `notifications/initialized` and other notification methods return HTTP 202 Accepted with empty body — NOT 200 with a JSON-RPC response
   558→- **MCP protocol version header**: Clients may send `MCP-Protocol-Version` header. If present and unsupported, respond with 400 Bad Request per spec
   559→- **SYNAPSE_PATH env var**: Controls WebSocket path segment (default `/synapse`). `SYNAPSE_PORT` controls port (default `9999`). Full URL: `ws://localhost:{SYNAPSE_PORT}{SYNAPSE_PATH}`
   560→- **orjson optional**: `protocol.py` and `mcp_server.py` use `orjson` for fast JSON with `OPT_SORT_KEYS` when installed, auto-fallback to stdlib `json`
